75 objectives indexed from 5 blogs, 2 of them with reports from more than one.

Planning a trip here? Check the [forecast](/weather-trail-conditions/popular-locations/vancouver-island)
and find [somewhere to sleep](/accommodation/vancouver-island) for the same area.

Each entry links every trip report, video, or GPS trace the indexed blogs published
for that objective. Hover a link to see the report’s own title, which is how
combined trips and traverses show what else they cover.

Where an objective is on one of the four tick-lists, that is marked after the links:
Kane and Nugara for scrambles and *Don’t Waste Your Time* for hikes, each carrying
the book’s own grade, and the 11,000ers carrying the peak’s elevation. None of the
three books is published online, and the 11,000ers is not a book at all, so every mark
links to [Adam Laycock’s page](https://adamlaycock.ca/lists/) for that objective,
which is the best canonical reference there is for one. Where there is a book, the
route description is in it.

The line under each entry says who puts it where. Where the sources agree, that is one
region with several names. Where they disagree, the objective is listed on every region
page named, and the line links the others: the blogs file Bow Peak under both Banff and the
Icefields Parkway, so it is on both pages.

A region marked *inferred* is not stated by any blog. It was worked out from where the
blogs place the objectives around it: those climbed in the same trip, those a report links
to, those near its trailhead, or those near where its name is on the map. Checked against
objectives the blogs do place, these are right about nine times in ten, so treat one as a
pointer rather than a fact.
One marked *weakly inferred* rests on thinner or split evidence — a single linked report,
a trailhead between two regions — and is only used where nothing else places the objective,
so it may be listed under each region it could be in.
Place-name positions are from the
[Canadian Geographical Names Database](https://natural-resources.canada.ca/maps-tools-publications/maps/geographical-names-canada),
under the [Open Government Licence – Canada](https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada),
and south of the border from the USGS
[Geographic Names Information System](https://www.usgs.gov/tools/geographic-names-information-system-gnis).
